newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures drift up, end with gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures drift up, end with gains.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures drifted higher during a holiday-shortened session to end with solid gains after a late sharp rally on light volume.
Trading in stock index contracts at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange ended at 1215 CST today and will be closed all day Wednesday for the Christmas holiday.
"We had a slight bias to the upside," said one S&P 500 trader on the floor of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
Overall, however, there were few outside influences to provide direction to the market on the day before the holiday.
Firmness in over-the-counter stocks provided some support, traders said, but the bond market barely moved, which left participants searching for direction.
March S&P 500 broke above a very minor resistance at a two-day downtrend line, that came in at about 756.00 today, and followthrough buying also helped send the nearby contract up.
Further buying after the close of cash stocks drove the March S&P contract up sharply and to new daily highs in a volatile rally in thin trading conditions.
Sentiment was mixed about near term direction, although light trading conditions are expected to persist through the New Years holiday.
Nikkei 225 declined, following the lead of Japanese stock overnight, but ended near session highs. March Nikkeis reached a new contract low on the fall.

At settlement, March S&P 500s were up 4.95 points at 759.05, Russell 2000s rose 1.60 point to 360.70, Value Line futures were up 1.50 point to 684.50, Nikkei 225 index futures eased 245.0 to 19325.0 and Midcap 400s rose 1.25 point to 255.75.
